item.title: Bahri Charters Five Supertankers as Rates Approach $200K/Day
item.description: Saudi Arabia's National Shipping Co. (Bahri) provisionally hired at least five supertankers as freight rates approach $200,000 per day, the highest since 2020. The bookings signal rising Saudi crude exports to Asia amid geopolitical tensions in the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Iran Loads 20 Million Barrels of Oil Onto Tankers as U.S. Military Buildup Intensifies
item.description: Iran loaded 20.1 million barrels of oil onto tankers from Kharg Island in just six days, tripling January's pace as the U.S. assembles its largest Middle East force since 2003. Satellite data shows tanker traffic doubled while storage tanks emptied rapidly.

item.title: Wind Giant Sees Strong U.S. Growth Despite Offshore Ban
item.description: EDP Renovaveis, the world's fourth-largest wind producer, reports 50% profit growth and optimism for U.S. expansion despite Trump's offshore wind ban. CEO says solar and battery storage are filling the gap as data center demand surges.

item.title: West Coast Gateway Ports Hold Ground Despite Tariff Turbulence and Policy Whiplash
item.description: The nation's two busiest container ports posted double-digit declines in January cargo volumes, but industry leaders say the dip reflects comparison against historic highs rather than structural weakness—even as Supreme Court intervention and rapid-fire tariff policy shifts inject fresh uncertainty into trans-Pacific trade lanes.

item.title: Mercy’s AIS Track Points to Panama Canal—Not Greenland—as Hospital Ship Steams South
item.description: One day after departing Alabama Shipyard, the hospital ship USNS Mercy is holding a steady southbound course through the central Gulf of Mexico — and AIS data is offering the clearest signal yet about where the 1,000-bed vessel may be headed.
